notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate #1. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: The kitchen and the tools in it

themes.theme: A kitchen you can find things in
themes.description: Stations, storage and why every working kitchen puts the knife, the board and the bin within one step of each other.
themes.transfer_check: Reorganise one real kitchen work area so a named dish can be made without crossing the room, and show the before and after.

bands.K–2: Help put dishes away in the right spot, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find a real kitchen tool where it belongs, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Organise a real kitchen area so tools are easy to find, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Set up a real kitchen workspace for efficient real cooking, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to organise a real kitchen for real efficiency.

themes.theme: The knife and the hand that holds it
themes.description: Grip, claw, board stability and the three cuts that cover most of cooking.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate the claw grip and produce even slices, dice and rough chop from real vegetables.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult cut something with a knife safely.
bands.3–5: Learn one safe knife grip, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Use a real knife safely with correct grip and technique, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use a real knife safely and skillfully on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else safe, skillful real knife technique.

themes.theme: Heat: what pans and ovens actually do
themes.description: Conduction, radiant heat and preheating — why the pan matters more than the recipe line that names it.
themes.transfer_check: Cook the same ingredient in a cold-start and a preheated pan and explain the difference you can see and taste.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a pan gets hot on the stove.
bands.3–5: Learn what heat does to real food, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain how a real pan or oven transfers heat to food, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Control real heat deliberately for a real cooking result, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to control real heat for a specific cooking outcome.

themes.theme: Fire, burns and the kitchen that bites
themes.description: Pan fires, steam, hot sugar and the responses that must be automatic before they are needed.
themes.transfer_check: Walk a real kitchen and state, for each hazard found, the correct first response — including why water never goes on an oil fire.

bands.K–2: Stay back from the stove unless an adult says it's okay.
bands.3–5: Know one kitchen fire safety rule, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real kitchen fire or burn hazard, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Respond correctly to a real kitchen burn or fire risk, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real safety rules for fire and burns in a kitchen.

themes.theme: Clean as you go
themes.description: The wash-rinse-sanitise order, cloths that spread rather than clean, and leaving a station ready for the next person.
themes.transfer_check: Cook one simple dish and finish with the station inspection-clean, narrating the order you cleaned in and why.

bands.K–2: Wipe up a small spill right away, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Clean up while cooking instead of leaving a mess, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Keep a real cooking space clean throughout a real task, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Clean as you go through a real full cooking session, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else why cleaning as you go matters in a real kitchen.

themes.theme: Cold: the fridge as a system
themes.description: Cold chain, shelf order, and why raw meat lives at the bottom.
themes.transfer_check: Audit a real fridge against safe shelf order and temperature, fix what is wrong, and log what you changed.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some food goes in the fridge.
bands.3–5: Learn why cold keeps real food safe, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify real correct fridge storage for different foods, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Organise a real fridge for safety and efficiency, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how a real fridge works as a food-safety system.

themes.theme: Measuring, tasting, adjusting
themes.description: Weights beat cups, tasting is a step not a treat, and salt-acid-fat-heat as the levers of adjustment.
themes.transfer_check: Season a bland base (soup or grain) to genuinely good by iterating taste-adjust-taste, recording each move you made.

bands.K–2: Measure an ingredient with an adult's help.
bands.3–5: Measure a real ingredient accurately, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Taste and adjust a real dish's seasoning, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Measure, taste and adjust a real dish confidently, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to taste and adjust a real dish like a cook.

themes.theme: The recipe as a plan, not a script
themes.description: Reading a recipe once through, mise en place, and knowing which lines are law and which are suggestion.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare full mise en place for a new recipe, then cook it without re-reading, marking beforehand the two lines that must not be improvised.

bands.K–2: Follow a simple recipe step with an adult.
bands.3–5: Follow a real simple recipe's steps in order, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Adapt a real recipe slightly based on what's available, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Treat a real recipe as a flexible plan, adapting it on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to read a real recipe as a plan, not a rulebook.

themes.theme: Tools you do not need
themes.description: What a knife, a pan and a pot replace, and how to judge a gadget before it takes the drawer.
themes.transfer_check: Cook a dish 'as seen' that normally uses a specialised gadget, using only basic tools, and compare results.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if a fancy gadget is really needed to cook.
bands.3–5: Learn that simple tools can do a real job well, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real unnecessary kitchen gadget, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Cook a real dish using only essential real tools, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why real basic tools often outperform gadgets.

themes.theme: A meal from a bare cupboard
themes.description: The pantry backbone — grain, allium, fat, acid, tinned protein — and building dinner when there is 'nothing in'.
themes.transfer_check: Cook a complete meal using only what is already in a real cupboard, listing what you used and what the meal cost.

bands.K–2: Help make a snack from what's in the kitchen, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Make a simple real meal from limited ingredients, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Cook a real meal from a real sparse set of ingredients, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Cook a real satisfying meal from a real bare cupboard, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to cook a real meal from what's actually available.

tracks.name: What food is: nutrition without the noise

themes.theme: Energy, and where it hides
themes.description: Calories as fuel, portion reality versus package fiction, and the drinks that are meals.
themes.transfer_check: Estimate the energy in one of your own typical days, then check against labels and a reference and report where you were most wrong.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult which foods give you energy to run and play.
bands.3–5: Name a real food that gives energy, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify where real energy hides in different real foods, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, where energy hides in a real meal.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to identify where real energy hides in food.

themes.theme: Protein, and who needs how much
themes.description: What protein is for, the plant and animal sources, and need across childhood, training, pregnancy and old age.
themes.transfer_check: Plan one real day of meals that meets the protein need of a named person unlike yourself, with sources shown.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult which foods help you grow strong.
bands.3–5: Name a real food that's high in protein, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify real protein needs for different people, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, how much protein a real person needs.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real evidence behind protein needs.

themes.theme: Carbohydrates: the fast and the slow
themes.description: Whole versus refined, fibre as the difference, and why the same sugar behaves differently inside an apple and a soda.
themes.transfer_check: Swap one refined staple in your week for a whole version and record the swap's cost, taste and how it held your hunger.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some snacks make you tired quickly.
bands.3–5: Learn the difference between fast and slow real carbs, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real fast versus real slow carbohydrate food, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real examples, the difference between fast and slow carbs.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real science behind fast and slow carbohydrates.

themes.theme: Fats: needed, chosen, hidden
themes.description: Cooking fats, essential fats and the fats that arrive uninvited in packaged food.
themes.transfer_check: Find the fat content and type in five packaged foods you actually eat and rank them against what you assumed.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some food needs oil or butter.
bands.3–5: Learn that fats are needed but should be chosen wisely, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real hidden source of fat in a food, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, how to choose real fats wisely.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real evidence on needed, chosen and hidden fats.

themes.theme: Reading a label in twenty seconds
themes.description: Per-100g versus per-portion, the ingredient list as a story told in descending order, and the claims on the front that mean nothing.
themes.transfer_check: Given two competing products, pick the better one using only the label, and defend the pick in four sentences.

bands.K–2: Look at the picture on a food label with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find the sugar amount on a real food label, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real food label quickly for key facts, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Read and compare real food labels quickly and accurately, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to read a real food label in twenty seconds.

themes.theme: Vitamins, minerals and the short list that runs low
themes.description: Iron, iodine, B12, vitamin D and calcium — who actually runs short, and the foods that fix it before pills do.
themes.transfer_check: For a named diet (vegan, low-dairy, low-sun), identify the likely gap and plan a week of real foods that closes it.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why eating vegetables matters.
bands.3–5: Name a real vitamin or mineral your body needs, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real nutrient people commonly run low on, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, which real nutrients run low most often.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real short list of nutrients worth watching.

themes.theme: Water, caffeine and what you drink all day
themes.description: Hydration reality versus myth, caffeine's arc through a day, and the quiet calories in what pours.
themes.transfer_check: Log everything you drink for three days and redesign the pattern with one change you can keep.

bands.K–2: Drink water when you're thirsty, with an adult's reminder.
bands.3–5: Learn that what you drink matters as much as food, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real drink's effect on hydration or energy, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate your own real daily drink choices, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real effects of common daily drinks.

themes.theme: Ultra-processed: what the term actually marks
themes.description: The formulation-versus-food distinction, why these products are engineered to be easy to keep eating, and where the evidence stands.
themes.transfer_check: Sort a week of your own shopping into whole, processed and ultra-processed, and name the one swap with the best effort-to-benefit ratio.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what makes some food come in a shiny package.
bands.3–5: Learn that some foods are made with many extra steps, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify what real makes a food 'ultra-processed', with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, what the term actually marks.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real evidence behind ultra-processed food.

themes.theme: Diets, claims and who profits
themes.description: Reading a nutrition claim like a Signal Reader: the study behind the headline, the influencer's sponsor, the before-after photo.
themes.transfer_check: Take one current diet claim from your feed, trace its evidence, and deliver a verdict a friend could act on.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if every food claim on TV is true.
bands.3–5: Learn that not every food claim is trustworthy, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real questionable diet claim and who benefits, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real diet claim critically, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to evaluate a real diet claim and its motives.

themes.theme: Eating patterns that hold
themes.description: Why patterns beat rules: regular meals, plates built around plants and protein, and change that survives a bad week.
themes.transfer_check: Design one realistic weekly eating pattern for yourself, follow it for a week, and report what held and what needs redesign.

bands.K–2: Eat regular meals with your family, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Keep a simple real eating routine for a week, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Build a real sustainable eating pattern, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build and maintain your own real sustainable eating pattern, on your own.
bands.11–12: Coach someone else on building a real eating pattern that actually holds.

tracks.name: Feeding people: planning, budget and the shop

themes.theme: The week on one page
themes.description: Meal planning that survives reality: anchor meals, flex nights and the leftovers written into the plan.
themes.transfer_check: Write a one-page plan for a real week, cook it, and mark what the plan got wrong for next time.

bands.K–2: Help pick meals for a few days, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help plan a simple real meal schedule for a week, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real week of meals on one page, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real full week of meals on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to plan a real week of meals efficiently.

themes.theme: The list, and the shop that follows it
themes.description: Building a list from the plan, the store's layout as persuasion, and endcaps designed to break your budget.
themes.transfer_check: Do one real shop from a written list, note every deviation and what triggered it, and total the cost of the deviations.

bands.K–2: Help write a shopping list with an adult.
bands.3–5: Write a real shopping list from a meal plan, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Shop using a real list without impulse extras, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Shop efficiently from a real list on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to shop from a real list without overspending.

themes.theme: Price per unit, not price per package
themes.description: Unit pricing, brand ladders and when the big pack is actually the expensive one.
themes.transfer_check: In a real aisle, find three cases where the obvious choice loses on unit price, with photos or figures.

bands.K–2: Compare two prices with an adult's help.
bands.3–5: Compare real prices of two similar items, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Calculate a real price per unit to compare options, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Compare real price per unit to find the best value, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to calculate and compare real price per unit.

themes.theme: Feeding four for less
themes.description: The cheap backbone proteins and grains, stretching meat, and the cuisines that mastered low-cost cooking long ago.
themes.transfer_check: Cook a family-sized meal under a set per-head budget and publish the costed recipe.

bands.K–2: Help make a meal stretch further, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Plan a real cheap meal for a family, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real affordable meal that feeds several people, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan and cook a real affordable meal for four or more, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to feed several real people affordably.

themes.theme: Cooking once, eating thrice
themes.description: Batch cooking, the fridge-freezer relay, and containers that make leftovers get eaten instead of feared.
themes.transfer_check: Batch-cook one base and serve it as three genuinely different meals across a week.

bands.K–2: Help save leftovers for later, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Cook extra food to eat again later, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real batch-cook that yields several real meals, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Batch-cook a real meal that stretches across several days, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to batch-cook efficiently for real multiple meals.

themes.theme: Waste: the food you paid for and threw away
themes.description: Date labels decoded (use-by versus best-before), storage that extends life, and the bin audit that changes behaviour.
themes.transfer_check: Audit one week of a real household's discarded food, price it, and change two storage or planning habits in response.

bands.K–2: Help use up leftover food instead of throwing it away, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Notice food that got wasted and why, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Reduce real food waste in a real kitchen, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Track and reduce your own real household's food waste, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real cost of food waste and how to cut it.

themes.theme: The seasons and the price of distance
themes.description: Why produce has a season and a price curve, and what freezing and tinning preserve of it.
themes.transfer_check: Compare the price and origin of one vegetable across fresh-in-season, fresh-out-of-season, frozen and tinned, and pick a policy for your household.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some fruit costs more in winter.
bands.3–5: Learn that food costs change with the real season, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real seasonal food's price pattern, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, how season and distance affect real price.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real economics of seasonal food pricing.

themes.theme: Feeding people who eat differently
themes.description: Allergy, faith, choice and medical diets at one table — planning one meal that works for everyone without cooking four dinners.
themes.transfer_check: Plan and cook one meal that safely serves a real mixed table (including one allergy or restriction), and explain your cross-contact controls.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a friend can't eat the same snack as you.
bands.3–5: Learn that some people need different real foods, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Plan a real meal that accommodates a real dietary need, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real meal for someone with a real different dietary need, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to plan for real diverse dietary needs.

themes.theme: When money runs short before the week does
themes.description: Food banks, community meals, benefits that cover food, and cooking through a genuinely empty stretch with dignity.
themes.transfer_check: Map the food support within reach of your own address — eligibility, hours, what to bring — into a half-page guide someone could use tomorrow.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens if food runs low before payday.
bands.3–5: Learn one way to stretch food when money is tight, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Plan a real meal on a real very tight remaining budget, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage real food needs when money runs short, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through managing real food needs on a shortfall.

themes.theme: Hosting: the meal as an event
themes.description: Scaling a recipe, the timeline written backwards from sitting down, and the dishes that let the host be at their own table.
themes.transfer_check: Host a real meal for four or more: publish your backwards timeline and serve everything within fifteen minutes of plan.

bands.K–2: Help set the table for guests, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help plan a simple meal for guests, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real meal event for guests, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan and host a real meal event for guests, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to plan and host a real successful meal event.

themes.theme: The invisible passengers
themes.description: Bacteria, viruses and toxins in food — which ones cause most illness, and the four controls (clean, separate, cook, chill) that stop them.
themes.transfer_check: For one real meal you cook, name the hazard most likely present at each step and the control you applied.

bands.K–2: Wash your hands before eating, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that germs can ride on real food, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real food safety risk from unseen contamination, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage real invisible food-safety risks in your own cooking, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real invisible risks food can carry.

themes.theme: Temperature: the danger zone
themes.description: The 5–60°C band, safe internal temperatures by food, and why a thermometer beats every rule of thumb.
themes.transfer_check: Cook a protein to its safe internal temperature verified with a real thermometer, and chart the cooling of the leftovers into safe storage.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why food shouldn't sit out too long.
bands.3–5: Learn that food left out too long can go bad, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify the real danger zone temperature range, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Keep real food out of the real danger zone, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real temperature danger zone and why it matters.

themes.theme: Cross-contact and the separate board
themes.description: Raw-to-ready pathways: boards, cloths, hands and the sink itself as the crossing points.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a raw-meat dish and a salad in one session with demonstrably zero cross-contact, narrating your controls.

bands.K–2: Use a different plate for raw and cooked food, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn why raw and cooked food need separate boards, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Prevent real cross-contact between raw and cooked food, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Practice real cross-contact prevention in your own cooking, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else why real cross-contact prevention matters.

themes.theme: Hands, hair and being clean enough to cook
themes.description: When handwashing actually matters, gloves as false comfort, and cooking while ill.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate the full handwash at the moments that require it during one cooking session, and name the two moments people skip.

bands.K–2: Wash your hands and tie back hair before cooking, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Follow real hygiene basics before cooking, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Practice real proper hygiene before and during cooking, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Maintain real proper hygiene throughout a real cooking session, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real hygiene standards for cooking safely.

themes.theme: Leftovers: the second life of a meal
themes.description: Cooling fast, reheating hot, the counting of days, and the foods that do not get a second chance (rice included).
themes.transfer_check: Take real leftovers through cool-store-reheat with times and temperatures logged, and bin-or-keep three fridge items with reasons.

bands.K–2: Help put leftovers in the fridge, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Store real leftovers safely, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Store and reheat real leftovers safely, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Store, reheat and judge real leftovers' safety on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to give real leftovers a safe second life.

themes.theme: Allergens: the eight that matter most
themes.description: The major allergens, reading them off labels and menus, and why 'a little bit' is not safe.
themes.transfer_check: Screen a real packaged meal and a restaurant menu for a named allergen, including the may-contain judgement call.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if a friend can't eat something you're having.
bands.3–5: Name a real common food allergen, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify the real eight major allergens, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Check a real recipe or product for real major allergens, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real eight major allergens and why they matter.

themes.theme: Preserving: the old technologies
themes.description: Salt, sugar, acid, heat and cold — how jam, pickles and tins actually work, and where home preserving goes dangerous (botulism and the low-acid jar).
themes.transfer_check: Make one safe high-acid preserve with correct process, and explain why the same jar of green beans would need a pressure canner.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how food used to be kept without a fridge.
bands.3–5: Learn one real old way of preserving food, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real traditional food preservation method, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real methods, how food was preserved before refrigeration.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else a real traditional food preservation technique.

themes.theme: Water you can cook with
themes.description: When tap water is the standard, when it is not (advisories, travel, wells), and making water safe.
themes.transfer_check: Find your own water supplier's latest quality report, and demonstrate one field method of making questionable water safe.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult before drinking water you're not sure about.
bands.3–5: Learn that some water needs to be treated before cooking, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real safe versus unsafe water source for cooking, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Judge a real water source's safety for cooking on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to make water safe for real cooking.

themes.theme: When food goes wrong anyway
themes.description: Recognising food poisoning, who is at real risk (pregnant, young, old, immunocompromised), and when it is a clinic call.
themes.transfer_check: Given three illness scenarios, decide home-care versus clinic versus emergency for each, and name the food rule that was likely broken.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult right away if you feel sick after eating.
bands.3–5: Know what to do if food seems to have made someone sick, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real foodborne illness sign and response, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Respond correctly to a real suspected foodborne illness, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real steps to take when food goes wrong.

themes.theme: Feeding the vulnerable
themes.description: The stricter rules for infants, pregnancy and elders: the foods excluded, the temperatures raised, the dates hardened.
themes.transfer_check: Adapt one family recipe so it is safe for a named vulnerable eater, listing each change and the rule behind it.

bands.K–2: Be extra careful feeding a baby or older relative, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that some people need extra food safety care, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify real extra precautions for a vulnerable person, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Apply real extra food safety precautions for a vulnerable person, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real extra care needed feeding vulnerable people.

tracks.name: Food, culture and the wider system

themes.theme: Where dinner comes from
themes.description: The chain from farm to plate — growing, processing, moving, selling — and the hands it passes through.
themes.transfer_check: Trace one item from your own plate back to its origin as far as evidence allows, documenting each link you can verify.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult where the food on your plate came from.
bands.3–5: Trace one real ingredient back to its real source, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Trace a real meal's ingredients back to their real origins, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Trace a real meal's full supply chain back to its origins, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to trace a real meal back to where it came from.

themes.theme: The dish that carries a people
themes.description: Food as heritage: why dishes migrate with people, and what a recipe preserves that a museum cannot.
themes.transfer_check: Learn one dish from someone of a tradition not your own, cook it to their approval, and record its story as they tell it.

bands.K–2: Learn about a food from your family's culture, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn the story behind a real cultural dish, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain what a real dish reveals about a real culture's history, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research and explain a real dish's cultural significance, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how a real dish carries a people's history.

themes.theme: The family recipe as an archive
themes.description: Oral recipes, the pinch and the handful, and writing down what an elder cooks before it is lost.
themes.transfer_check: Document one real family or community recipe from its keeper — quantities, technique and story — into a form a stranger could cook from.

bands.K–2: Ask a family member for a recipe they love, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Write down a real family recipe, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Record a real family recipe with its story, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Document a real family recipe as a piece of family history, on your own.
bands.11–12: Help someone else preserve a real family recipe as a living archive.

themes.theme: The table as a practice
themes.description: Shared meals and what they measurably do for households, and the hospitality codes different cultures build around food.
themes.transfer_check: Run a device-free shared meal with real people, applying one hospitality practice from a culture you researched, and reflect on what changed.

bands.K–2: Sit down and eat a meal together with family, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Notice what happens at a real shared family meal, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Explain the real value of a shared table practice, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build a real regular shared-table practice in your own life, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why the real table matters as a practice, not just eating.

themes.theme: What food costs the planet
themes.description: Land, water and emissions by food type — the honest hierarchy, and why the biggest lever is usually waste, not the exotic swap.
themes.transfer_check: Rank five of your staple foods by environmental footprint using published data, and make one evidence-based change you can sustain.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if growing food uses water and land.
bands.3–5: Learn that different foods use different resources, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real food's real environmental cost, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, the real environmental cost of a food choice.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real trade-offs in food's environmental cost.

themes.theme: The people who grow and serve
themes.description: Farm labour, kitchen labour and delivery labour: the working conditions inside the price of a meal.
themes.transfer_check: Investigate the labour behind one food you buy weekly and present what its price does and does not pay for.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who grows the food you eat.
bands.3–5: Name a real job involved in growing or serving food, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify several real roles in the real food supply chain, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research the real people and labor behind a real meal, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real labor behind the food we eat.

themes.theme: Food deserts and food swamps
themes.description: Why some neighbourhoods have six chicken shops and no greengrocer, and what access actually determines about diet.
themes.transfer_check: Map real food access within walking distance of two different addresses in your area and compare what a week's healthy shop would take at each.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if every neighbourhood has a grocery store nearby.
bands.3–5: Learn that some places lack real access to healthy food, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real food desert or food swamp and its cause, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Research a real food access issue in a real community, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advocate for a real solution to a real food access problem.

themes.theme: Marketing on a plate
themes.description: How food is sold — to children especially: placement, packaging, cartoon spokesmen and the school-adjacent economy.
themes.transfer_check: Collect five food marketing techniques aimed at children from real shelves or screens and redesign one advert to sell the honest version.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why a cereal box looks so exciting.
bands.3–5: Notice how real food packaging tries to get your attention, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real marketing technique used to sell food, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate real food marketing critically before buying, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real food marketing shapes what we choose.

themes.theme: Growing something you eat
themes.description: One pot, one windowsill, one bed: the shortest possible supply chain and what tending it teaches.
themes.transfer_check: Grow one edible plant from start to harvest, log its care, and cook what you grew.

bands.K–2: Plant a seed and water it, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Grow a simple plant from seed and watch it, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Grow a real edible plant successfully, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Grow real food on your own, from planting to harvest.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to grow a real food plant successfully.

themes.theme: Feeding the future
themes.description: How the food system might feed ten billion — precision agriculture, alternative proteins, redistribution — and how to judge each claim.
themes.transfer_check: Take one 'future of food' claim, examine the strongest evidence for and against, and stake a defensible position in one page.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how there will be enough food for everyone someday.
bands.3–5: Learn that feeding everyone in the future takes planning, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real challenge in feeding a growing population, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real evidence, a real challenge in future food systems.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real challenges of feeding the future.
